Keep `export const GET = trackedRoute("route.subscription-reminders", 86400, run)` and maxDuration.

runRegistry() gains the option `daily?: boolean`. With it, the due test for an 86,400 job is not jobDue() but: due when last_ok_at is null or before the start of today (UTC), and its tries today are under 3. For that the first read also selects last_ok_at, day and day_tries, and each write sets `day = current_date, day_tries = case when j.day = current_date then j.day_tries + 1 else 1 end` (both in record() and in the idle batch; for non-daily prefixes the two columns are written the same way and never read). So a second call of the route on the same day runs only the jobs that failed or were not reached, and never a job more than three times a day. A daily job that fails three days running still emails the admins through the existing FAILING_AFTER rule.
cronJobs gains `day: date("day")` (nullable) and `dayTries: integer("day_tries").notNull().default(0)`. Run `pnpm db:generate`.

migration.notes: Two files. Generated (pnpm db:generate): commerce.cron_jobs gains day date and day_tries integer not null default 0 (a small table, not hot). Custom: replaces commerce.cron_due() with one more row for the daily route's same-day retry. Running code keeps working: old code ignores the two columns, and until the new route is live a retry call simply runs the old route once more, which the old route tolerates only because each reminder goes once whoever calls; to be safe, ship the route change and the migration in the same push (CI applies the migration first, the deploy follows within minutes, and cron_due() names the daily route only after 07:30 UTC, so push outside 07:00 to 09:00 UTC). CI applies it after every check passes and before the deploy (docs/ci-migrations.md); never apply it by hand. After the deploy check the Supabase security and performance advisors for project ybsozesfuxuitoacntfo and record the file's version in docs/decisions.md under Migration versions.
